summary: Defines a standard way to store the configuration and results of traceroute measurements. It describes an information model that separates configuration from results and then an XML data model based on it. This is a Proposed Standard.

eli5.summary: When many people record their trips, it helps if everyone uses the same notebook layout. This memo gives a common layout for saving the route a traceroute test finds.

subtitle: A common way to record how a traceroute was set up and what it found, as an information model and an XML format.

tldr.problem: Many measurement efforts use traceroute, but each stores its settings and results differently, and the standard IPPM delay and loss metrics do not apply to what traceroute reports.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines an information model that splits configuration elements from result elements and links them with a shared TestName, then encodes it as an XML schema for storing and exchanging traceroute measurements.
tldr.outcome: Traceroute results from different tools and operating systems can be stored in one structure, with the tool and OS recorded so results can be compared.

today: RFC 5388 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata for this RFC lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Standardize Traceroute Storage
sections.content:
Traceroutes are used by many measurement efforts, either on their own or to get path information that supports other measurements. The RFC says the standard IPPM metrics for delay, connectivity and loss do not apply to what the traceroute tool returns. The only way to compare results is to store the operating system and the name and version of the tool alongside them.

The RFC therefore defines one standard way to store the configuration and the results of traceroute measurements, using an XML schema. It does not specify a traceroute tool or a procedure for storing the data.
sections.eli5: Everybody who tests a network route writes down their notes in a different style. This memo picks one style so the notes can be compared.

sections.title: How Traceroute Works
sections.content:
Traceroute discovers the hop-by-hop path from a source to a destination, plus the round trip time (RTT) to each hop. Typically it sends UDP probes with specific time-to-live (TTL) values and tries to get an ICMP TIME_EXCEEDED response from each gateway on the path.

The first probes have TTL 1. Each hop decreases the TTL, and a hop that sees zero rejects the probe and normally replies, which reveals its address and the RTT. The TTL is then raised by one for each next hop, until an ICMP PORT_UNREACHABLE message shows the destination was reached or the configured maximum hop count is hit.

Some tools use ICMP Echoes instead, but many routers do not return ICMP messages about ICMP messages, so the RFC recommends basing implementations on UDP datagrams.

Per hop, tools report the hop index, the symbolic address if resolved, the IP address, and an RTT per probe. A probe with no answer in time shows as an asterisk, which the model records as the string RoundTripTimeNotAvailable.
sections.eli5: Traceroute sends little messages that are allowed to travel only one step, then two steps, then three, and each stopping point says hello. That way you learn every stop on the road to a destination.

sections.title: The Information Model
sections.content:
The model is built from information elements, each described by a name, a description, a data type and units. The data types include string, string255, inetAddress, boolean, unsignedInt, unsignedShort, unsignedByte, and probesType, whose values are UDP, TCP and ICMP.

A measurement is a traceRoute element holding one optional RequestMetadata element and any number of Measurement elements. Each Measurement holds an optional MeasurementMetadata element and any number of MeasurementResult elements.

RequestMetadata says what was asked for, so it can be sent to several nodes to run the same measurement. MeasurementMetadata says what was actually used. Both use the same type in the XML schema. If RequestMetadata is omitted, all the requested parameters were used and MeasurementMetadata lists them.

Different mixes of these elements in a file serve different purposes: a request only, one measurement, repeated runs with the same settings, or several measurements at once.
sections.eli5: Each saved test has a page for what you planned, a page for what you really did, and pages for what you found.

sections.title: Configuration and Result Elements
sections.content:
The configuration elements are named with a Ctl prefix. They cover the target and source address, the probe data size, the timeout per probe, CtlProbesPerHop, the base port, CtlMaxTtl and CtlInitialTtl, the Differentiated Services field, the interface index, the don't-fragment flag, a limit on consecutive timeouts, and CtlType, which says whether probes are TCP, UDP, ICMP or another type.

A MeasurementResult has a start time, the target address, the probe results, and an end time. The probe results hold 1 to 255 hop elements. Each hop holds 1 to 10 probe elements and an optional HopRawOutputData element.

Each probe records the hop address, an optional DNS name, up to 255 MPLS label stack entries, the round trip time, a response status and a timestamp.

The TestName element is the common identifier that ties configuration to results. The elements OSName, OSVersion, ToolName and ToolVersion are there so results can be compared.
sections.eli5: The notes list the settings used, such as how many tries per stop and how long to wait, and for each stop the address, the name, and how long the reply took.

sections.title: Why XML and the Schema
sections.content:
The RFC weighs a few options. The DISMAN-TRACEROUTE-MIB module (RFC 4560) is well supported in network management systems but, as a general storage and transmission format, it is not easily applicable. An IPFIX-based binary format would face obstacles because that architecture targets passively measured flows.

XML gives clean structure and syntax checking, is supported by many tools, and is readable to a degree. Its cost is resource use, which the RFC does not expect to matter given the expected data volumes. The schema uses a template approach where configuration is metadata referenced by results through TestName, and the RFC says it is compatible with a schema used by the Open Grid Forum, with a simple one-to-one transformation between them.

Section 7 gives the schema, which should use UTF-8, and documents SHOULD carry an XML declaration with the version and encoding. The RFC also contains appendices on default traceroute settings, known problems, differences from the MIB module, and worked XML examples.
sections.eli5: The authors picked a text format that people and programs can both read. It is a little bulky, but the amount of data is small, so that is fine.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Running traceroute puts traffic on the network, and it can be abused for denial-of-service attacks disguised as legitimate measurement. Measurement parameters MUST be carefully selected so the extra traffic is trivial. Methodologies SHOULD reduce the chance that measurement traffic can be told apart from normal traffic, so routers cannot give it special treatment.

The stored information is not considered highly sensitive, but it may reveal network paths, routing states, IP addresses and round trip times that operators want to protect. The RFC RECOMMENDS appropriate protection for privacy, integrity and authenticity when sending it over a network, and secure authentication and authorization for stored data.
sections.eli5: Testing a route sends real traffic, so do not send too much. The notes can also show how a network is laid out, so keep them away from strangers.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: Two URNs were registered, following RFC 3688. They are urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:traceroute-1.0 for the namespace and urn:ietf:params:xml:schema:traceroute-1.0 for the schema. The registrant contact is the IESG.
sections.eli5: The format got an official name tag so everyone can point to the same one.
